modules.title: Foundational AI Concepts
modules.text:
Before you can understand how AI systems like ChatGPT, Claude, or any intelligent product works,
there are five foundational concepts you need to know.
These are not optional extras — every AI
application you will ever encounter is built on top of them.
This module walks through each one in
plain language, no technical background required.
By the end, you will have a clear mental model of
how AI "thinks," how it finds relevant information, and how teams choose what kind of AI to use.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of AI systems like ChatGPT and Claude?

options.text: To replace human workers in all industries
To perform tasks that require human-like intelligence
To create entirely new industries
To eliminate the need for data analysis

questions.explanation: AI systems like ChatGPT and Claude are designed to perform tasks that require human-like intelligence, such as understanding and generating natural language, problem-solving, and decision-making. They do not replace human workers in all industries, nor do they create new industries or eliminate the need for data analysis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the five foundational concepts covered in this module?

options.text: Machine Learning
Neural Networks
Data Processing
Natural Language Processing

questions.explanation: The module covers five foundational concepts, but data processing is not explicitly listed as one of them. The concepts include machine learning, neural networks, natural language processing, and others that are not listed here. Data processing is a broader term and may be part of the overall AI workflow but is not one of the five specific concepts mentioned.

questions.question_text: What is the main goal of understanding foundational AI concepts?

options.text: To develop your own AI systems
To understand how AI systems work and make informed decisions
To become an AI engineer
To replace traditional software development

questions.explanation: The main goal of understanding foundational AI concepts is to gain a clear mental model of how AI systems work, how they find relevant information, and how teams choose what kind of AI to use. This understanding helps in making informed decisions about AI applications without requiring a technical background.

modules.title: Core AI Concepts
modules.text:
Some Complex Topics:
If you are interested to learn more about AI you must learn the following 5 concepts:
Neural Networks:
- A system of connected nodes arranged in layers that process data
- Data goes in one end, flows through layers, and a result comes out
- Training adjusts internal weights each time the model gets something wrong
- After enough training it handles examples it has never seen before
- All modern AI — LLMs, image generators, voice models — are neural networks
Frontier Models vs Open source models:
- Frontier models are the most powerful proprietary models (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini)
- Accessed via API and charged per use; weights are kept private by the company
- Open source models have publicly released weights (Llama, Mistral, Qwen).
The models
used by the PhillipCapital chgatbot is open source.
- Open source gives full control and can be cheaper at scale but needs own infrastructure
- Choice depends on capability needed, control required, and budget
Embedding Model:
- Converts text (or images, audio) into a list of numbers called a vector
- Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together in numerical space
- "Dog" and "puppy" will be close; "dog" and "skyscraper" will be far apart
- Turns unstructured language into something computers can compare mathematically
- Foundation of search, recommendations, and any "find similar content" feature
Cosine Similarity:
- Measures how similar two vectors are by calculating the angle between them
- Score of 1.0 = identical meaning; -1.0 = opposite; 0 = unrelated
- Uses angle not straight-line distance — unaffected by length of text
- Used in vector search to find the most relevant content for a query
Vector database
- A database built to store embeddings and search through them at speed
- Returns the closest matching vectors to a query — called nearest neighbour search
- Unlike SQL, finds fuzzy meaning-based matches rather than exact keyword matches
- Popular options: Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector
- The backbone of any RAG system connecting AI to your private documents
These five concepts form the foundation of everything in modern AI.

slides.script: Now, let's look at how embedding models work. These models convert text, images, or audio into numerical vectors. Similar meanings result in vectors that are close together in numerical space, while dissimilar concepts are farther apart. For example, 'dog' and 'puppy' have close vectors, but 'dog' and 'skyscraper' are far apart. This transformation allows computers to compare unstructured data mathematically, forming the foundation for search, recommendations, and content similarity features.

It is used in vector search to find the most relevant content for a query.

A score of 1.0 means identical meaning, while -1.0 indicates opposite meanings. Unlike distance-based measures, cosine similarity focuses on the angle, making it unaffected by text length. This makes it ideal for vector search, helping find the most relevant content for any query.

modules.title: Client Meeting Process & Relationship Management
modules.text:
Client Meetings — Approach, Pitch & Follow-up
● Pre-meeting preparation:
○ Research the client via MCA21, ZaubaCorp, or LinkedIn
○ Review existing portfolio or lead history in PhillipX
○ Prepare 2–3 relevant product ideas — never go empty-handed
○ Carry visiting card, brochures, and a note-taking tool
● During the meeting — 70/30 rule (70% listening, 30% talking):
○ Open with context: understand what the client wants to achieve
○ Ask needs discovery questions: investment goals, time horizon, risk appetite,
current investments
○ Never pitch in the first meeting unless the client specifically asks
○ Build rapport before product — ask about their business/profession first
○ End with a clear next step: confirm a follow-up date for a proposal
● What NOT to do: walk in and immediately pitch, make price predictions or return
guarantees, lie about product performance, take phone orders verbally without logging
● Follow-up and relationship building:
○ Call every client at least once per week — to connect, not to pitch
○ Read market news daily — be able to have an informed 5-minute conversation
○ Speak in themes, not tips: e.g., "IT sector has been volatile this quarter"
○ Acknowledge important dates: business anniversaries, major life events
○ Tell clients about compounding — time in the market is the message
SWOT & Personal Revenue Strategy
● Strengths to identify: client servicing, communication, network, product depth
● Weaknesses to acknowledge: market knowledge gaps, activity discipline, follow-up
consistency, compliance awareness
● Two strategies to pick from (commit to one):
○ Client-wise: choose one segment (Retail / Affluent / HNI) and go deep
○ Product-wise: choose 2–3 products you know best, find the right client type
● 4 patterns every RM must avoid:
○ Stop Acquiring — relying on the existing book; new blood is always needed
○ Cave Under Pressure — violating guidelines when targets are missed; always
ends worse
○ Stop Learning — not keeping up with markets and regulatory changes; credibility
falls fast
○ Organisational Dishonesty — misreporting meetings, faking activities; discipline
builds long careers
Dormant Account Revival
● Four reasons accounts go dormant:
○ Age/Life stage — reposition to fixed income, bonds, SLB
○ Loss — acknowledge loss first, rebuild trust, do not pitch immediately
○ Goal not achieved — review new goals, fresh conversation
○ Lost relationship — personal call from new RM, no pitch in first 2 calls
● Revival process:
○ Pull account history from PhillipX: last transaction, last MOM, last contact
○ Identify the reason for dormancy
○ Close the gap — address why it went dormant before pitching anything
○ Propose a fresh start: understand where the client is today
○ Do NOT lead with product in the first revival call
● Post-account-opening non-negotiables:
○ Flag any unusually large trade to the dealing desk
○ All trades must be recorded — no verbal or informal confirmations
○ No orders over the phone — all orders through the approved system
○ Initiate all communication in English
○ Answer dealing room phone within one ring, always with "PhillipCapital"

modules.text:
● Converts text (or images, audio) into a list of numbers called a vector
● Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together in numerical space

● Turns unstructured language into something computers can compare mathematically
● Foundation of search, recommendations, and any "find similar content" feature
● Measures how similar two vectors are by calculating the angle between them

● Uses angle not straight-line distance — unaffected by length of text
● Used in vector search to find the most relevant content for a query

bullets.text: Converts text (or images, audio) into a list of numbers called a vector

slides.script: We'll begin by understanding how text is transformed into vectors. This process converts words, images, or audio into numerical lists that represent their meaning. slides.script: Now let's explore how similar meanings translate to vector proximity. Words with related meanings, like 'dog' and 'puppy,' produce vectors that are numerically close. modules.title: Welcome to PhillipX – Why CRM Matters
modules.text:
Module 1: Welcome to PhillipX – Why CRM Matters
● PhillipX is your digital field companion, built on ERPNext and customised for
PhillipCapital
● You will learn to: log in securely with biometric and SSO, manage leads from creation to
conversion, and log meetings with GPS
● Authentication uses two factors: SSO (PhillipCapital Active Directory credentials) +
Biometric (fingerprint on Android / Face ID on iOS)
● Every client interaction must be logged in PhillipX to ensure traceability, manager
visibility, automated client communications, and personal productivity

modules.title: Navigating the App – Login, Dashboard & Quick Links
modules.text:
Module 2: Navigating the App – Login, Dashboard & Quick Links
● Login: Open PhillipX → enter PhillipCapital User ID and password → complete biometric
authentication (fingerprint on Android / Face ID on iPhone)
● Dashboard has three key daily widgets: Today's Meetings, Tomorrow's Meetings, and
Today's Due Tasks
● Quick Links provide shortcuts to: Lead, Daily Activity, Attendance, MOM, Meeting, and
Tasks
● Footer navigation bar is persistent across all screens — use it to jump between sections
without pressing Back
● Sales Managers and HODs see two tabs: Self (own schedule) and CRM (entire team
view); RMs see only their own view

modules.title: Leads – Creating, Viewing and Managing
modules.text:
Module 3: Leads – Creating, Viewing and Managing
● A lead is any person who might become a PhillipCapital client — every lead has a full
record in PhillipX (contact details, product interests, meetings, notes)
● To create a lead: tap Leads in Quick Links → tap Add → fill mandatory fields: First
Name, Source, Status, Salesperson, Mobile Number, City
● Additional fields: Name, City, State, Country, Lead Product Interest (multi-select), Approx
Investment Amount
● On saving: status auto-sets to Open and a follow-up meeting is auto-created for that day
● Lead status flow: Open → Interested → Converted; Do-Not-Contact requires a
mandatory Lost Status reason (Poor Fit, Pricing, Budget Constraints, etc.) — cannot be
skipped
● Lead assignment: auto-assigned by pin code/round robin, assigned by manager, or bulk
imported
● Only the assigned RM and their manager can see the lead; re-assignment allowed within
the department hierarchy only
● Pending leads from resigned salespersons are flagged on the Manager Dashboard with
a re-assignment option

modules.title: Scheduling, Check-in, Check-out & MOM
modules.text:
Module 4: Scheduling, Check-in, Check-out & MOM
● Two meeting types:
○ Online Meeting — video or phone; no GPS required
○ Offline Meeting — in-person client visit; GPS check-in and check-out required
● To schedule: open a lead → tap Meetings → tap New Meeting → select type → set date
and time; system warns for scheduling conflicts; client contact auto-added as external
participant
● GPS Check In (Offline only): open the meeting → tap Check In; app captures GPS
coordinates and converts to address via Google Maps; no photo required
● Check Out: tap Check Out when meeting ends; system calculates time on site → change
status to Completed
● If you forgot to check out: manually set status to Completed and edit check-out time —
manager can see these edits
● Each offline meeting requires its own independent check-in/check-out cycle
● MOM (Minutes of Meeting) has four sections: Attendees, Meeting Objective, Key
Discussion Points, Next Steps
● Lead field is the only mandatory MOM field; Salesperson auto-fills; MOM can be edited
any time — no lock or deadline
● After MOM: optional Send Feedback Request to Client checkbox — client receives a
short rating form via email
● System auto-sends a reminder email to the client 24 hours before the meeting — no
manual action needed

modules.title: Tasks, Notes & Daily Activities
modules.text:
Module 5: Tasks, Notes & Daily Activities
● Tasks: open any lead → scroll to Tasks → tap New Task → set due date; task appears in
Today's Due Tasks widget on dashboard
● Tasks can also be created without linking to a lead — useful for internal follow-ups
● Notes: open a lead → Notes section → tap New Note → type or tap the microphone to
record a voice note
● Voice notes are saved and play back inside the note record; only one voice note plays at
a time; text comments can be added after saving a voice note
● Searching for a lead: type any part of the name (first, last, or middle); system ignores
salutations like Mr.
or Mrs.
● Daily Activity: logs time-based work; available on web app via Reports menu; not
available on mobile in current version

modules.title: Conversion & Onboarding
modules.text:
Module 6: Conversion & Onboarding
● When a prospect is ready: change lead status to Converted

○ Discounted Broking (TOG)
○ Self-Assisted — client completes KYC independently
○ RM-Assisted — RM completes KYC on the client's behalf
● System generates an eKYC link after path selection
● Link can be sent directly from the CRM via email or WhatsApp — no manual handoff
required
● Client receives the link, completes the process, and their account is opened
automatically

Artificial Intelligence is a branch of computer science that

modules.title: Core AI Concepts
modules.text:
Some Complex Topics:
If you are interested to learn more about AI you must learn the following 5 concepts:
Neural Networks:
- A system of connected nodes arranged in layers that process data
- Data goes in one end, flows through layers, and a result comes out
- Training adjusts internal weights each time the model gets something wrong
- After enough training it handles examples it has never seen before
- All modern AI — LLMs, image generators, voice models — are neural networks
Neural network image
Frontier Models vs Open source models:
- Frontier models are the most powerful proprietary models (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini)
- Accessed via API and charged per use; weights are kept private by the company
- Open source models have publicly released weights (Llama, Mistral, Qwen).
The models
used by the PhillipCapital chgatbot is open source.
- Open source gives full control and can be cheaper at scale but needs own infrastructure
- Choice depends on capability needed, control required, and budget
chatgpt
Embedding Model:
- Converts text (or images, audio) into a list of numbers called a vector
- Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together in numerical space
- "Dog" and "puppy" will be close; "dog" and "skyscraper" will be far apart
- Turns unstructured language into something computers can compare mathematically
- Foundation of search, recommendations, and any "find similar content" feature
embedding example representation
Cosine Similarity:
- Measures how similar two vectors are by calculating the angle between them
- Score of 1.0 = identical meaning; -1.0 = opposite; 0 = unrelated
- Uses angle not straight-line distance — unaffected by length of text
- Used in vector search to find the most relevant content for a query
Cosine similarity example
Vector database
- A database built to store embeddings and search through them at speed
- Returns the closest matching vectors to a query — called nearest neighbour search
- Unlike SQL, finds fuzzy meaning-based matches rather than exact keyword matches
- Popular options: Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector
- The backbone of any RAG system connecting AI to your private documents
Vector database flow
These five concepts form the foundation of everything in modern AI.
A neural network is the
engine.
An embedding model is how meaning gets turned into numbers.
Cosine similarity is
how those numbers get compared.
A vector database is where they get stored and searched.
And understanding the difference between frontier and open source models tells you which
engine to pick for any job.
Once these click, the intermediate concepts — RAG, agents, transformers, orchestration —
become much easier to understand because they are all just these five ideas combined in
different ways.
That is what the next module covers.

- Unlike SQL, finds fuzzy meaning-based matches rather than exact keyword matches

These five concepts form the foundation of everything in modern AI.
A neural network is the
engine.
An embedding model is how meaning gets turned into numbers.
Cosine similarity is
how those numbers get compared.
A vector database is where they get stored and searched.
And understanding the difference between frontier and open source models tells you which
engine to pick for any job.
Once these click, the intermediate concepts — RAG, agents, transformers, orchestration —
become much easier to understand because they are all just these five ideas combined in
different ways.
That is what the next module covers.

bullets.text: Neural networks are systems of connected nodes arranged in layers that process data.
Data flows through layers, with results emerging after processing.
Training adjusts internal weights to improve accuracy over time.
After sufficient training, models can handle new examples they haven't seen before.
All modern AI systems, including LLMs and image generators, are based on neural networks.

lessons.lesson_title: Compare model types and use cases

bullets.text: Frontier models are the most powerful proprietary models, such as GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini.
These models are accessed via API and charged per use, with private weights.
Open source models have publicly released weights, like Llama, Mistral, and Qwen.
The PhillipCapital chatbot uses an open source model.
Open source models offer full control and can be cost-effective at scale but require infrastructure.
Model choice depends on required capabilities, control needs, and budget.
Embedding models convert text, images, or audio into numerical vectors.
Similar meanings result in vectors that are numerically close.
Words like 'dog' and 'puppy' produce close vectors, while 'dog' and 'skyscraper' are far apart.
Embedding models transform unstructured data into a format computers can compare mathematically.
They form the foundation for search, recommendations, and content similarity features.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors to determine similarity.
A score of 1.0 indicates identical meaning, while -1.0 indicates opposite meanings.
A score of 0 means the vectors are unrelated.
Cosine similarity uses angle rather than distance, making it independent of text length.
It is used in vector search to find the most relevant content for a query.
Vector databases store embeddings and enable fast searches.
They return the closest matching vectors to a query, known as nearest neighbor search.
Unlike SQL, they find meaning-based matches rather than exact keyword matches.
Popular vector database options include Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, and pgvector.
Vector databases are essential for RAG systems connecting AI to private documents.

modules.text:
Module 4: Scheduling, Check-in, Check-out & MOM
● Two meeting types:
○ Online Meeting — video or phone; no GPS required
○ Offline Meeting — in-person client visit; GPS check-in and check-out required
● To schedule: open a lead → tap Meetings → tap New Meeting → select type → set date
and time; system warns for scheduling conflicts; client contact auto-added as external
participant
● GPS Check In (Offline only): open the meeting → tap Check In; app captures GPS
coordinates and converts to address via Google Maps; no photo required
● Check Out: tap Check Out when meeting ends; system calculates time on site → change
status to Completed
● If you forgot to check out: manually set status to Completed and edit check-out time —
manager can see these edits
● Each offline meeting requires its own independent check-in/check-out cycle
● MOM (Minutes of Meeting) has four sections: Attendees, Meeting Objective, Key
Discussion Points, Next Steps
● Lead field is the only mandatory MOM field; Salesperson auto-fills; MOM can be edited
any time — no lock or deadline
● After MOM: optional Send Feedback Request to Client checkbox — client receives a
short rating form via email
● System auto-sends a reminder email to the client 24 hours before the meeting — no
manual action needed
